system.name: LAGER
system.one_liner: A post-hoc, plug-and-play framework that aggregates cross-layer score-token logits of a frozen LLM judge into an expected score aligned with human ratings.

content.variant_note: a problem panel on two scoring prompts, then a decoder-only LLM chain with one block zoomed into its layers and read out through a shared LM head
content.argues: Equal vanilla scores hide different score distributions, so reading all layers' score-token logits and taking the expected score judges responses more finely and closer to human scores.
content.subject: Two prompts with the same vanilla score but different score histograms, then LAGER's layer-wise logit aggregation inside a decoder-only LLM.

lessons.what_to_learn: Expose a hidden difference with a two-case problem panel: two cases with the same surface output, a small histogram under each output, and a tick or cross against the reference. Then draw the fix as one model chain, a zoom wedge opening the repeated block, and dotted taps from every layer to a shared head.
lessons.suits: Methods that read internal states or output distributions of a model, where a single surface output hides informative signal.

tags: two panels split by a dashed line

evidence: vanilla score overlooks informative score distributions by relying solely on the top-probability score token
instead of relying on a single token, the full probability distribution over score candidates can be leveraged
LAGER fully considers candidate score probabilities and aggregates cross-layer logits

summary: LAGER is a post-hoc, plug-and-play framework that improves how well an LLM judge's point-wise scores agree with human scores, without changing the frozen backbone. Figure 1 has two panels split by a dashed line. In (a), two prompts that differ only in the response go through one robot judge and both return Score: 7; histograms of the score-token probabilities underneath look very different, and a tick and a cross compare the vanilla score with the reference score. In (b), the decoder-only model is drawn as a chain (embedding, N decoder layers, LM head, softmax); a dashed wedge opens the layers, dotted arrows send every layer's hidden state to one LM head, candidate-score logits are extracted, weighted and summed, and the final score is the expected value.
summary_zh: LAGER 是用 LLM 内部各层表示改进「LLM 评委」打分的后处理框架。图左(a)用两个同为 7 分、概率分布却迥异的提示说明问题；图右(b)展开解码器各层，取各层候选分数 logits 加权求和，再以期望得到最终分数。
notes: Prior kinds kept. The Embedding and LM_Head trapezoids are gradient-filled bitmaps in the extraction; they are modules, so they are listed as elements, not icons. The reference and vanilla score boxes are tied to prompts A and B by position only.
